newsitem.title: UK: UK's Waldegrave casts doubt on quick UK EMU entry.
newsitem.headline: UK's Waldegrave casts doubt on quick UK EMU entry.

text.p: Chief Secretary to the Treasury, William Waldegrave, said on Tuesday it was increasingly unlikely that Britain would join the first wave of countries entering a single currency in 1999.
"As each day goes by...it is increasingly unlikely that Britain will be there at the start," Waldegrave told a financial industry award ceremony.
Waldegrave was speaking at a ceremony giving awards to brokerage houses and fund managers in the 1997 Reuters survey of European larger companies.
He noted that a cabinet meeting last week reaffirmed that a decision on single currency membership would be taken on the basis of Britain's national interest.

He said it was vital that international business put itself into a position to cope with EMU and said he believed the City of London financial community could rise to the challenge of being either in or out.
